title: Organizational Vocabulary Layer (OVL)
description: Schema for an organization's OVL — the semantic alignment layer that ensures agents on different models process the same concepts consistently. Part of the Agentic Governance Framework by Indira Réquiz, 2026.

ovl_id.description: Unique identifier for this OVL instance

effective_date.description: Date from which this OVL version is active

approved_by.description: Underwriter of Liability who approved this version. No term can become PRESCRIBED without human approval.

status.description: PRESCRIBED: active, injected into all agent contexts in this domain. CANDIDATE: proposed, pending human approval. DEPRECATED: no longer active, kept for audit trail.

domain.description: Business domain this term applies to (e.g., 'finance', 'legal', 'operations', 'all')

counterexamples.description: Examples of incorrect usage this definition aims to prevent

divergence_history.description: Record of cross-model divergences that motivated this definition (dynamic mode history)

injection_template.description: Exact text to inject into agent context when this term is relevant. Wrap in <ovl> tags.

terms.definition: A task or message classified as urgent requires a human decision-maker to be notified within 4 hours and a resolution or escalation within 8 business hours. It does not imply immediate interruption of ongoing work.
examples: A customer contract dispute > $50K is urgent
A system outage affecting >10% of users is urgent
counterexamples: A routine report delayed by 1 hour is NOT urgent
A question requiring same-day response is NOT urgent — use 'priority'

divergence_history.discrepancy: claude interpreted 'urgent' as 'respond within 4h'; gpt-4o interpreted as 'respond within same business day'. Led to 3 missed escalations.

terms.injection_template: <ovl>ORGANIZATIONAL DEFINITION — 'urgent': Requires human notification within 4 hours and resolution/escalation within 8 business hours. NOT equivalent to 'immediate' or 'same-day'.</ovl>

terms.definition: A document, action, or output is 'approved' only when it has received explicit written sign-off from an authorized Underwriter of Liability for its domain. Implicit approval (silence, verbal confirmation, or automated pass) does not constitute 'approved' status.
examples: An invoice marked as approved with digital signature from Finance Director
A contract with explicit approval timestamp in the Ledger
counterexamples: An output that passed automated testing is NOT approved — it is 'validated'
A task completed without rejection is NOT approved
terms.injection_template: <ovl>ORGANIZATIONAL DEFINITION — 'approved': Requires explicit written sign-off from authorized Underwriter. Automated validation pass ≠ approved. Silence ≠ approved.</ovl>

terms.definition: Revenue figures in all reports default to USD at the period-average exchange rate from the 1st to last business day of the reporting period. Source: ECB reference rates via Snowflake fx_rates table. Do not use spot rates unless explicitly requested.
examples: Q1 2026 EUR revenue: convert at average EUR/USD rate Jan 2 – Mar 31 2026
terms.injection_template: <ovl>FINANCIAL STANDARD — Revenue reporting: use USD at period-average FX rate (ECB reference, Snowflake fx_rates table). Period = first to last business day of reporting period.</ovl>
